# collectype

> CollecType is a modern, type-safe collection utility for TypeScript with fluent, chainable filtering, sorting, pagination, and pipeline composition.

## Project Links

- Home: https://maduhaime.github.io/collectype/
- API reference: https://maduhaime.github.io/collectype/modules
- Changelog: https://github.com/maduhaime/collectype/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/collectype
- Source: https://github.com/maduhaime/collectype

## Core Architecture

CollecType is built around two primary abstractions:

1. `Collection<T, F>`
- A typed wrapper over your raw items array.
- Exposes `collection.items` (raw/original items) and `collection.fn` (functions instance).

2. Functions classes (`BaseFunctions<T>`, `FullFunctions<T>`, or custom subclasses)
- `BaseFunctions` provides core query mechanics (`where`, `sort`, `page`, `pipe`, `begin`, `end`, etc.).
- `FullFunctions` extends `BaseFunctions` and exposes built-in typed filters by data family.

### Important Behavioral Rule

Functions methods are chainable and mutate the internal working set on the same instance (`this`).
For independent queries, instantiate a fresh functions/collection instance.

---

## AI Usage Rules

### Always Prefer Typed Family Methods

For typed filtering, use methods aligned to the field type family:

- `string*` for `string` fields
- `number*` for `number` fields
- `boolean*` for `boolean` fields
- `bigint*` for `bigint` fields
- `date*` for `Date` fields
- `array*` for array fields
- `map*` for `Map` fields
- `set*` for `Set` fields
- `object*` for object fields
- `query*` for `URLSearchParams` and `URL` query scenarios
- `url*` for `URL` fields

Do not invent method names. Use methods that exist on `BaseFunctions`/`FullFunctions` or custom subclasses.

### Query Family Special Case

Query methods accept both `URLSearchParams` and `URL` values. `URL` inputs are evaluated through query semantics.

### Use `where` for Domain-Specific Logic

When built-in typed methods do not match the need, use `where((item) => boolean)` in custom function classes.

---

## BaseFunctions Contract

Core methods:

- Chainable: `all()`, `where()`, `sort()`, `page()`, `pipe()`, `begin()`, `end()`
- Read-only state: `items`, `count`, `info`

### `info` Tracking

`info` provides current execution state:

- `count`: current item count
- `steps`: tracked step names (`'_unknown_'` for unnamed filters)
- `sort`: current sorting metadata
- `page`: current pagination metadata

### Pipe Constraints

- `pipe('...')` executes expression chains dynamically.
- Reserved/internal methods are blocked in pipe expressions.
- `page()` is not available in pipe expressions; use direct chaining.

---

## FullFunctions Scope

`FullFunctions` extends `BaseFunctions` and currently exposes **266 strongly-typed filters**.

Data families covered:

- Arrays
- BigInt
- Boolean
- Date
- Map
- Number
- Object
- Query
- Set
- String
- URL

Method names are intentionally explicit and family-prefixed (for discoverability and type-guided usage).

---

## Composition Pattern (Recommended)

Use factory composition in custom functions classes:

- Extend `BaseFunctions<T>` or `FullFunctions<T>`
- Add project/domain methods
- Optionally compose with exported factories (e.g., `stringComparisonFactory`, `numberRangeFactory`)

This pattern keeps business rules explicit, testable, and reusable.

---

## Type Safety Expectations

- Field names are constrained by TypeScript utility typing (family-compatible keys only).
- Prefer compiler-guided usage over casts.
- Do not silence type errors with `any` if an equivalent typed method exists.

---

## Practical Guidance for AI Generation

1. Start with `Collection(items, FullFunctions)` when broad filtering is needed.
2. Use `Collection(items, BaseFunctions)` plus custom subclass methods for domain workflows.
3. Keep chains readable and deterministic.
4. Use fresh instances for independent test assertions because chains are stateful.
5. Prefer direct chaining over `pipe` unless dynamic runtime expressions are required.

---

## Example

```typescript
import { Collection, FullFunctions } from 'collectype';

type Person = {
  name: string;
  age: number;
  hobbies?: string[];
  website?: URL;
};

const people: Person[] = [
  { name: 'Alice', age: 30, hobbies: ['fishing'], website: new URL('https://example.com/?tag=pro') },
  { name: 'Bob', age: 17, hobbies: ['gaming'], website: new URL('https://example.com/') },
];

const c = new Collection(people, FullFunctions);

const adultsWithTag = c.fn
  .numberGreaterOrEqual('age', 18)
  .queryContainsKey('website', 'tag')
  .items;
```

---

## Scope

CollecType is a TypeScript library distributed via npm and documented on GitHub/GitHub Pages. It is not a hosted service.
